sentences.en: Hi everybody, welcome to The Rest is History and Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《历史其余部分》（The Rest is History），祝大家新年快乐。

sentences.en: And welcome back to the recording of the live show that Tom and I did at the Royal Albert Hall in London on the 4th of May 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到我们 2025 年 5 月 4 日在伦敦皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅举办的现场演出录音。

sentences.en: Now on Monday, you should have heard the first half of that show, which was the episode on the Russian composer Tchaikovsky.
sentences.zh: 在周一，大家应该已经听过这场演出前半部分的内容，那是一集关于俄罗斯作曲家柴可夫斯基的节目。

sentences.en: And in today's episode, we'll be broadcasting the second half of that show.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将播出这场演出的后半部分。

sentences.en: And this is in one of the most influential, incendiary and controversial composers, indeed artists of any kind in world history.
sentences.zh: 本期主角是世界历史上最具影响力、最具煽动性和争议性的作曲家之一，甚至可以说是任何流派的艺术家中都首屈一指的人物。

sentences.en: And the name of that man is Richard Wagner.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是理查德·瓦格纳。

sentences.en: Thank you, thank you very much.
Tom, amazing to see that some people are still here.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，很高兴看到还有人留在这里。

sentences.en: So, that was, as many of you will know,
sentences.zh: 那么，正如大家所知，刚才那首曲子是——

sentences.en: From the opera Die Valkyrie, The Valkyrie, The Divine Shield Maiden, and our Divine Shield Maidens tonight were Christine Burrus,
sentences.zh: 选自歌剧《女武神》，也就是女武神，神圣的盾牌少女，今晚我们神圣的盾牌少女有：克里斯蒂娜·布鲁斯、

sentences.en: Marie Wynne Williams, Ella de Jong, Rebecca Afonwi-Jones,
sentences.zh: 玛丽·韦恩·威廉姆斯、埃拉·德容、丽贝卡·阿丰维-琼斯、
凯蒂·史蒂文森以及玛尔塔·丰塔内莱-西蒙斯。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we ended part one with a banger, and we've begun part two with another absolute banger.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们在第一部分结束时放了一首神曲，而第二部分的开场又是另一首绝对的神曲。

sentences.en: One of the most instantly recognisable pieces of music ever written.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来辨识度最高的音乐作品之一。

sentences.en: So, if any of you are planning to strafe a Vietnamese village from a helicopter, this is the ideal accompaniment, as you will know if you've seen the film Apocalypse Now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你们当中有人正计划开着直升机去扫射一个越南村庄，这绝对是理想的配乐，看过电影《现代启示录》的人自然会懂。

sentences.en: It is, of course, emblematic of the man who wrote it, the composer who is the subject of our second half, and that is Richard Wagner.
sentences.zh: 它当然是其创作者的象征，也就是我们下半场节目的主角、作曲家理查德·瓦格纳。

sentences.en: And, Tom, in the first half we talked about how Tchaikovsky was described by his governess as being as brittle as porcelain,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在上半场我们谈到柴可夫斯基曾被他的家庭教师形容得像瓷器一样易碎，

sentences.en: and that is not a description that anyone has ever applied to Richard Wagner.
sentences.zh: 而这个词从来没有人用来形容过理查德·瓦格纳。

sentences.en: No, no, not at all, because Wagner, in all honesty, was a bit of a bruiser.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有，因为说实话，瓦格纳是个十足的狠角色。

sentences.en: This is a man who essentially bent the whole of the 19th century to his own purposes.
sentences.zh: 这个人基本上是按照自己的意愿把整个 19 世纪玩弄于股掌之间。

sentences.en: And, in fact, I would go so far as to say that he is the single most controversial composer in the entire history of music.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我甚至想说，他是整个音乐史上最具争议的作曲家。

sentences.en: I mean, remember that this is a man who wrote savagely anti-Semitic essays, who was Adolf Hitler's favourite composer,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，别忘了这个人曾撰写过极度反犹太主义的文章，是阿道夫·希特勒最喜欢的作曲家，

sentences.en: and whose operas to this day have never been staged in the state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 而且他的歌剧至今未能在以色列国上演。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so it's not really surprising that there's a slight whiff of sulfur about Wagner's public reputation.
sentences.zh: 对啊，所以人们对瓦格纳的公众声誉带有一丝硫磺般的恶臭也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: I think the word we use, Tom, is pungent.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得我们用的那个词叫“刺鼻”。

sentences.en: And so I think the question is, does his anti-Semitism, which is absolutely gross and palpable, it is absolutely out there, does it taint his music?
sentences.zh: 所以我想问题在于，他的反犹太主义——这是绝对粗俗且显而易见的，是公开摆在台面上的——是否玷污了他的音乐？

sentences.en: Are his operas, in some sense, a prefiguring of Nazism?
sentences.zh: 他的歌剧在某种意义上是否是纳粹主义的预演？

sentences.en: And this is an argument that has been raging among Wagner scholars since really the late 60s, and it's obviously a very important, a very heated debate,
sentences.zh: 这个争论在瓦格纳学者中自 60 年代末以来就一直甚嚣尘上，显然这是一个非常重要、非常激烈的话题，

sentences.en: and we will be coming to it in due course.
But it's absolutely not the only reason why Wagner matters and why he is a completely worthy theme for a history podcast, let alone a music podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对不是瓦格纳重要、且他完全配得上成为历史播客（更不用说音乐播客）主题的唯一原因。

sentences.en: And I think the reason why Wagner casts such a kind of outsized shadow over the 20th century is because he's such a massive, massive influence on the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我认为瓦格纳之所以对 20 世纪投下如此巨大的阴影，是因为他对 19 世纪产生了极其巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And in fact, I think it's hard to think of any composer, perhaps any creative artist, whose influence on the 19th century, the cultural influence, was more titanic than Wagner's.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得很难想到还有哪个作曲家，甚至哪个创意艺术家，其对 19 世纪的文化影响力能超过瓦格纳的泰坦般的影响。

sentences.en: So some of you may have come a year ago when we did Mozart and Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 在座有些人可能一年前听过我们讲莫扎特和贝多芬的那场。

sentences.en: Now, Beethoven was Wagner's favorite composer, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 贝多芬是瓦格纳最喜欢的作曲家，对吧？

sentences.en: And Beethoven had started a process that Wagner carried to its extreme, which is to take music out of the court, out of the palace, and to take it to the public,
sentences.zh: 贝多芬开启了一个进程，而瓦格纳将其推向了极致，那就是把音乐请出宫廷、请出王宫，带给大众，

sentences.en: to take it into the heart of public life.
sentences.zh: 将其融入公共生活的核心。

sentences.en: Where it still is to this day.
sentences.zh: 音乐至今依然留在那里。

sentences.en: So here we are in the Royal Albert Hall, but this is not a palace, this is a kind of public theater.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在身处皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅，但这可不是宫廷，这是一种公共剧场。

sentences.en: And Wagner is really the midwife of institutions like this,
sentences.zh: 而瓦格纳正是这类机构的催生者，

sentences.en: partly because he was such a genius, partly because his music was so influential, but also, and I think just as significantly,
sentences.zh: 一部分原因在于他是个天才，一部分原因在于他的音乐极具影响力，但同样重要的原因是，

sentences.en: because Wagner never for a moment doubts that he is a genius.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳从不怀疑自己是个天才。

sentences.en: Dominic, I mean, we have experience of colossal egotism, don't we?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我的意思是，我们对极度的自负并不陌生，对吧？
确实，从我们的制作人身上就能看出来。

sentences.en: But Wagner's egotism is off the scale.
sentences.zh: 但瓦格纳的自负简直突破天际。

sentences.en: But the thing is that not only, I mean, unlike us, not only is Wagner's egotism justified, but it enables him to bulldoze his way through obstructions
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，与我们不同的是，瓦格纳的自负不仅是名副其实的，而且它还赋予了他横扫一切障碍的力量，

sentences.en: that would absolutely have halted a less self-confident and less assertive composer.
sentences.zh: 换作一个不够自信、不够强势的作曲家，这些障碍早就让他停步不前了。

sentences.en: So that by the end of his life, it's not Wagner who is paying court to royalty, but the other way around.
sentences.zh: 所以在他的晚年，不是瓦格纳去向皇室献殷勤，而是反过来了。

sentences.en: It is kings and emperors who are paying court to Wagner.
sentences.zh: 是国王和皇帝们反过来向瓦格纳献殷勤。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Tom, I think there's also another reason why Wagner is such an extraordinary subject for an event like this.
sentences.zh: 是的，汤姆，我觉得瓦格纳成为这样一场活动的非凡主题还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: If you compare him with Tchaikovsky, or indeed with Mozart and Beethoven, or with Johann Sebastian Bach, or most composers that you choose to mention,
sentences.zh: 如果你把他与柴可夫斯基，或者莫扎特和贝多芬，又或是约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·巴赫，以及你随口能说出的绝大多数作曲家相比，

sentences.en: there are all sorts of flamboyant biographical details in Wagner's life that have no equivalent in the lives of other composers.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳的生活中充满了各种浮华的传记细节，这是其他作曲家的人生中所没有的。

sentences.en: And often kind of unexpected details.
sentences.zh: 而且往往是一些意想不到的细节。

sentences.en: So to look at one of them,
Wagner, compared to every other composer who is kind of his equal, is an unbelievably late developer.
sentences.zh: 与他同等级别的其他所有作曲家相比，瓦格纳是一个大器晚成得不可思议的人。

sentences.en: So he's born in Leipzig in Saxony in 1813.
sentences.zh: 他于 1813 年出生在萨克森的莱比锡。

sentences.en: So what's that, about 25, 30 years before Tchaikovsky?
sentences.zh: 那是怎样？比柴可夫斯基早了大约 25 到 30 年？

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's just a few months after Napoleon has begun his retreat from Moscow.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且就在拿破仑开始从莫斯科撤退几个月之后。

sentences.en: So the Napoleonic Wars are raging all around Wagner when he's born.
sentences.zh: 所以瓦格纳出生的时候，拿破仑战争正在他身边肆虐。

sentences.en: And baby Richard, which it's very hard to think of Wagner as baby Richard, but he was at one point, he is the last of nine children fathered by a man who then promptly dies
sentences.zh: 小理查德——把瓦格纳想象成小理查德很难，但他确实也有过那么小的时候——他是某个男人生下的九个孩子中的老幺，而那个男人不久后便去世了，
以一种非常具有瓦格纳风格的方式。

sentences.en: And his mother then marries again, and Wagner later in life seems to have wondered whether his stepfather had actually been his father.
sentences.zh: 然后他的母亲再婚了，瓦格纳在晚年似乎怀疑过他的继父实际上是不是他的亲生父亲。

sentences.en: And as we will see, this theme of people with kind of uncertain paternity is a theme that runs throughout Wagner's operas.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，这种身世不明之人的主题贯穿了瓦格纳的整个歌剧生涯。

sentences.en: And something really important about this stepfather though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不过关于这个继父，有一点非常重要，汤姆。

sentences.en: So his stepfather was not a musical man, but he was a man of the theatre.
sentences.zh: 他的继父不是个音乐中人，但却是个戏剧中人。

sentences.en: And that was to really shape Richard Wagner's life.
sentences.zh: 这一点真正塑造了理查德·瓦格纳的一生。

sentences.en: And lots of Wagner's elder brothers were also very involved in the theatre.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳的许多哥哥也都深度参与了戏剧行业。

sentences.en: And I think because of this kind of familial influence,
sentences.zh: 我想正是由于这种家庭环境的影响，

sentences.en: Wagner grows up as a boy and then a young man who is at least as obsessed by the theatre as he is by music.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳在童年和青年时期，对戏剧的痴迷程度至少不亚于对音乐的痴迷。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very proficient at music.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的音乐造诣很高。

sentences.en: But he's not an absolute maestro in the way that Mozart is from the kind of, well, the age of three months or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但他并不是那种打从三个月大（或者类似年纪）起就展现出绝对大师风范的莫扎特。

sentences.en: And so you may wonder, this being so, why does Wagner aspire to become a composer?
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，既然如此，为什么瓦格纳渴望成为一名作曲家呢？

sentences.en: And I think the answer essentially is because he wants to set plays to music.
sentences.zh: 我想答案本质上是因为他想为戏剧配乐。

sentences.en: And that's why Wagner is drawn to opera above all, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么瓦格纳最被歌剧吸引的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: Because when we think of Wagner, we don't think of any other musical form really, but his operas.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们想到瓦格纳时，我们想到的基本上除了他的歌剧之外，别无他物。

sentences.en: I mean, that's essentially pretty much exclusively what he writes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他写的东西基本上全都是这个。

sentences.en: And his interest in opera is not just as a composer.
sentences.zh: 他对歌剧的兴趣不仅限于作为一个作曲家。

sentences.en: He wants to write the librettos.
He wants to design the theatre.
He essentially wants to control every last detail of the production.
sentences.zh: 他基本上想要掌控制作的每一个最后细节。

sentences.en: But I guess the problem for somebody like that is gargantuan ambitions, but does he have gargantuan means and opportunities?
sentences.zh: 但我想这样的人面临的问题是：他有着庞大无比的野心，可他有庞大无比的资源和机会吗？

sentences.en: Well, in his teens, in his 20s, and then going into his 30s, no, he absolutely doesn't because he's from a very humble background, relatively speaking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在他十几岁、二十几岁一直到三十几岁时，绝对没有，因为他相对而言出身非常卑微。

sentences.en: And all the powers of patronage in Germany at this point still lie overwhelmingly with courts.
sentences.zh: 当时德国所有的赞助权仍然主要掌握在宫廷手中。

sentences.en: And Germany is a kind of patchwork of kingdoms and princedoms and archbishoprics and so on.
sentences.zh: 德国当时是由各种王国、公国、大主教区等拼凑而成的碎布拼图。

sentences.en: And these are the people who are really effectively the only employers that a musician can look to.
sentences.zh: 这些人才是音乐家实际上唯二可以依靠的雇主。

sentences.en: And so this is the course, the slightly humiliating course from Wagner's own perspective that he has to follow as a young man.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是年轻时的瓦格纳不得不遵循的道路，从他自己的角度来看，这是一条略带屈辱的道路。

sentences.en: And so if we look at him in, let's take a year at random,
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看他，比如说随便挑一个年份，

sentences.en: 1848, when Wagner is 35, he's kind of done okay by the standards of most musicians.
sentences.zh: 1848 年，当时瓦格纳 35 岁，按大多数音乐家的标准来看，他过得还算可以。

sentences.en: He's head of music at the Royal Court of Saxony in Dresden.
sentences.zh: 他是德累斯顿萨克森王家宫廷的音乐总监。

sentences.en: And he's miserable because he feels that his status as court musician is a humiliating one.
sentences.zh: 他痛苦是因为他觉得身为宫廷音乐家，自己的地位十分屈辱。

sentences.en: On special musical occasions, he has to wear a blue coat with a kind of harp on the collar.
sentences.zh: 在特殊的音乐场合，他必须穿一件领口带有某种竖琴图案的蓝色制服外衣。

sentences.en: And to Wagner, this is like the livery of a servant.
sentences.zh: 对瓦格纳来说，这就像是仆人的号衣。
他认为那里简直无可救药。

sentences.en: He wants to pull it down and build a new one.
And he hates the musical tastes of his employer and of the locals because they are essentially interested in operettas.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌他的雇主和当地人的音乐品味，因为他们本质上只对轻歌剧感兴趣。

sentences.en: And this is not where Wagner is at all because what Wagner wants to do is write titanic operas
sentences.zh: 这根本不是瓦格纳所追求的，因为瓦格纳想写的是气势磅礴的歌剧，

sentences.en: about mythology, about men of destiny,
sentences.zh: 关于神话，关于命运之子，

sentences.en: Well, you mentioned revolution, Tom, and you claimed you'd chosen a year at random, and I think that was a lie.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你提到了革命，而且你说你是随便挑了一个年份，我觉得你在撒谎。

sentences.en: So 1848, as some of you will know, is the year of revolution in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以正如在座各位所知，1848 年是欧洲的革命之年。

sentences.en: And by May 1849, Tom, incredible scenes.
sentences.zh: 到了 1849 年 5 月，汤姆，那场面简直难以置信。

sentences.en: The storm clouds of revolution are gathering above Dresden and Saxony and putting Wagner in their shadow.
sentences.zh: 革命的暴风雨云正聚集在德累斯顿和萨克森的上空，将瓦格纳笼罩其中。

sentences.en: And Wagner couldn't be happier about this.
sentences.zh: 而瓦格纳对此高兴得不得了。

sentences.en: And it may surprise people who think of Wagner as being, well, you know, let's face it, right wing.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让那些认为瓦格纳是——好吧，让我们面对现实吧，右翼的人感到惊讶。
因为实际上，这么说并不公平。

sentences.en: He has certain right wing opinions, can't deny that.
sentences.zh: 他确实有某些右翼观点，这不可否认。

sentences.en: But in his essentials, he's a bit of an anarchiSt.
